prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
answers:
[action] Wrote `regex.txt` with one regex, verified with a Python harness (`tmp_test.py`) over the sample log plus 25 crafted edge cases.

Structure and assumptions:
- `^(?=.*IP...)` line lookahead: line must contain a valid IPv4. `.*?` then walks to the date; `(?!.*DATE)` negative lookahead forces it to be the last valid date on the line. `.` never crosses newlines, so each match stays on its line; `re.findall` yields the single capture group (the date) in line order.
- IPv4: each octet `25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9]` (0-255, no leading zeros).
- Date: 31-day months `0[13578]|1[02]`, 30-day months `0[469]|11`, February up to 29 in every year (no leap-year rule, per brief).
- Adjacency: `(?<![0-9A-Za-z])` / `(?![0-9A-Za-z])` around both date and IP, exactly the brief's "letter or digit"; punctuation like `[10.12.0.7]` or `(2026-04-03)` still counts.
- Assumptions: year is any 4 digits; "last date" means last valid one, invalid pseudo-dates like 2026-04-31 are ignored, not blockers; exactly one capture group so findall returns dates only.

[result] Test run: `whole log: ['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05', '2026-04-02']`, `group count: 1 fails: 0`. That matches the expected last-date-per-IP-line for server.log (line 1 → 2026-04-01, line 3 → 2026-04-05, line 5 → 2026-04-02; lines 2 and 4 give nothing). Edge cases cover leading-zero and >255 octets, alnum adjacency on both sides, Feb 29/30, 30/31-day months, month 00/13, and multi-line ordering.

One real bug was caught and fixed by the tests: an initial `0[13-9]` month class wrongly let 2026-04-31 match; the failing output drove the fix to `0[13578]|1[02]`, after which all cases pass.

[next] Nothing open; `regex.txt` holds the regex alone. No browser or apps were opened.
